chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who sold goods to another man, so the buyer took possession of the goods and did not pay the price. Then the buyer died and the goods remained exactly as they were. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the goods are exactly as they were, they are returned to the owner of the goods.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for the creditors to dispute them.'

Ibn Abi Umayr said, 'And the interpretation of that is that there is no inheritance for her until the debt is paid. Rather, he left a thousand dirhams, and upon him was a debt of a thousand and five hundred dirhams for her and for the man. So her share is one third of the thousand, and for the man is two thirds.'

key_terms.قَائِمٌ بِعَيْنِهِ: remaining exactly as they were / intact and identifiable

ai.seo_question: What happens to specific goods bought on credit if the buyer dies before paying?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the priority of returning specific, unpaid goods to the seller over general creditors, a principle rooted in the concept of 'return of the eye' (Radd al-Ayn) within Shia jurisprudence. The accompanying note illustrates the practical application of debt settlement, where the specific debt amount is deducted from the estate before the residual wealth is divided among heirs according to their prescribed shares.
